item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Tinubu’s 2024 record does not show a clean, explicit pattern of using welfare, food, housing, or benefits as a formal loyalty-punishment system. The stronger evidence points to broad, programmatic welfare measures, but there are also real patronage-risk signals and a separate pattern of punitive state response to dissent.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Title:** Nigeria restarts cash transfers to cushion hardship caused by reforms  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via MarketScreener  
  **Date:** February 26, 2024  
  **URL:** [https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Nigeria-restarts-cash-transfers-to-cushion-hardship-caused-by-reforms-46031196/](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Nigeria-restarts-cash-transfers-to-cushion-hardship-caused-by-reforms-46031196/)  
  **Claim:** The government approved resuming direct cash transfers to 12 million vulnerable households to cushion cost-of-living pain. That is broad social protection, not a clear loyalty-based reward scheme.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.7

- **Title:** In Detail: The Student Loan (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2024  
  **Publisher:** State House, Nigeria  
  **Date:** April 4, 2024  
  **URL:** [https://statehouse.gov.ng/in-detail-the-student-loan-access-to-higher-education-act-2024/](https://statehouse.gov.ng/in-detail-the-student-loan-access-to-higher-education-act-2024/)  
  **Claim:** Tinubu signed a student-loan law that broadened eligibility, created NELFUND, and emphasized access to higher education and skills acquisition. This supports a universalist welfare frame rather than selective political patronage.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.7

- **Title:** President Tinubu Approves Takeoff of Consumer Credit Scheme  
  **Publisher:** State House, Nigeria  
  **Date:** April 24, 2024  
  **URL:** [https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-approves-takeoff-of-consumer-credit-scheme/](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-approves-takeoff-of-consumer-credit-scheme/)  
  **Claim:** The administration presented consumer credit as a broad social-mobility tool for homes, vehicles, education, and healthcare. Again, this reads as general access policy, not a loyalty filter.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.7

- **Title:** Reps blame agric ministry for delay in sharing Tinubu’s palliative  
  **Publisher:** The Guardian Nigeria  
  **Date:** January 9, 2024  
  **URL:** [https://guardian.ng/news/reps-blame-agric-ministry-for-delay-in-sharing-tinubus-palliative/](https://guardian.ng/news/reps-blame-agric-ministry-for-delay-in-sharing-tinubus-palliative/)  
  **Claim:** Rice palliatives were released to lawmakers for distribution to constituents, which makes the channel discretionary and politically exposed even if the stated aim was relief. This is not proof of partisan favoritism, but it is susceptible to patronage-style use.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.7

- **Title:** Tinubu under fire for appointing son-in-law head of housing agency  
  **Publisher:** BusinessDay  
  **Date:** February 21, 2024  
  **URL:** [https://businessday.ng/news/article/tinubu-under-fire-for-appointing-son-in-law-head-of-housing-agency/](https://businessday.ng/news/article/tinubu-under-fire-for-appointing-son-in-law-head-of-housing-agency/)  
  **Claim:** The appointment of Tinubu’s son-in-law to head the Federal Housing Authority drew explicit nepotism accusations. This is the clearest 2024 housing-related patronage signal and cuts against a clean anti-favoritism reading.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.7

- **Title:** Nigeria charges 76, including minors, with treason after August protests  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** November 1, 2024  
  **URL:** [https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000)  
  **Claim:** After cost-of-living protests, the state escalated to treason charges against 76 people, including minors. This is not a welfare-policy example, but it is strong evidence of punitive political control rather than neutral treatment of dissent.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.7

**Search Gap**
I did not find reliable 2024 reporting that Tinubu explicitly used permits or public-sector jobs as a documented loyalty test or punishment tool. The evidence is mostly indirect: broad welfare programs on the positive side, a few patronage-risk distribution channels and a nepotism-flavored housing appointment, and then a separate pattern of coercive punishment toward protesters.
